items.title: Ant Colony Development Wiki
items.text:
Ant Colony is a small, finishable, single-player 2D side-view colony simulation built in Unity 6. The design centres on persistent individual ants, physical work, destructible terrain, and an authored-content-first development approach.

This wiki is a readable development companion to the repository's authoritative documents. It describes the confirmed design, the current implementation, and the evidence behind milestone status without treating planned work as finished gameplay.

Current accepted baseline

Milestone 3.4C: player Colony HUD and developer UI separation.

Latest implemented slice

Milestone 3.5B: loose-only excavation output — pending manual acceptance.

Engine

Unity 6000.3.8f1, 2D URP, C#, new Input System.

Status vocabulary

Planned means approved design or roadmap intent, not code. Implemented means the repository contains the feature. Automated tested means named tests were executed successfully. Accepted means the required manual Unity checks were also confirmed. These labels are not interchangeable.

items.title: WV-B1 region boundary
items.text: WV-B1 does not add autonomous cross-view routing or Surface jobs. Existing survival and Colony-work evaluators continue to advance persistent ant needs from the shared clock, but they issue Colony-local navigation/work only when the ant's authoritative residency is the Colony region. A Surface-resident ant can receive direct player Surface movement or a manual entrance request; it cannot accidentally claim a Colony Vector2Int destination from the inactive view. Existing Colony jobs and reservations are not reset by camera switching or representation handoff.

items.title: Approved job model
items.text:
Future autonomous work uses a per-ant matrix of priorities 1–4 plus Disabled. The highest eligible priority wins before the closest reachable job by path cost. Skills change efficiency; they do not override player-assigned priority.

Ants may also receive temporary explicit orders. Critical survival may interrupt ordinary work at a safe point. Valid partial progress persists, and exclusive reservations prevent two ants from consuming or owning the same work target. Drafted survival intervention remains unresolved.

items.title: Current implementation
items.text:
Milestones through 3.3D are accepted, and 3.4A extends that foundation with physical Background construction:

  • Every ant record owns independent priorities for Excavation, Surface Preparation, Construction, Hauling, Foraging, Production, Combat, and Brood Care.
  • ColonyJobRegistry owns synthetic job identity, target, status, reservation, progress, and failure state outside GameObjects.
  • Highest enabled priority is evaluated before actual A* route cost. Equal costs use stable deterministic ties.
  • Evaluations inspect at most 32 candidates per priority, are staggered, and back off for 2/4/8 seconds on failure.
  • SyntheticColonyJobOrder remains as a regression fixture. Real designations use ExcavationJobOrder through the same registry, selector, motor, adjacency, priority and interruption seams.
  • Excavate mode accepts eligible foreground Solids by world coordinate, supports bounded area drags, and blocks ordinary selection/orders while active.
  • Soil and Stone extraction uses a stable job-keyed transaction. The complete yield always becomes loose output at the excavated cell; excavation never mutates inventory or assigns hauling. Output failure preserves the Solid; successful removal preserves Background and refreshes one visual/collision/navigation locality.
  • Work takes a provisional four simulation hours, uses Rested and relevant-skill speed, and awards proportional XP only for committed progress.
  • Player orders and critical survival pause work and release ownership while preserving progress. Ordinary survival waits for active work.
  • Explicit player pickup reserves one loose drop quantity and travels through the same shared navigation/adjacency seam. This is an order, not an autonomous Hauling job.
  • Autonomous Hauling jobs reserve loose source quantity and compatible Material Storage capacity, then use the same motor to visit valid adjacent source and destination anchors. Already-carried Soil/Stone creates an owner-only self-deposit task.
  • Actual A* travel cost selects the closest reachable compatible storage with deterministic ties. Disabled Hauling blocks dynamic claims; critical survival and explicit player orders interrupt safely.
  • The development scene exposes deterministic job, excavation and loose-drop fixtures plus priority, inventory, cancellation, reset, and diagnostic controls.
  • Background Conversion designations create real Construction jobs. The exclusive builder uses inventory first, otherwise reserves reachable storage/drop material, stages it at the site, performs timed work and commits the Background transaction.
  • A construction builder with no usable inventory capacity temporarily unloads unnecessary cargo through a reusable recovery operation: closest reachable reserved storage first, validated recoverable current-anchor drop second, then automatic resumption of the same job. Critical survival and player orders may interrupt this state safely.
  • Construction interruption preserves progress, carried material and staged material. Cancellation releases reservations and exposes staged material as a recoverable drop.

Foraging is reserved for discovering resource locations, Extraction for physically removing resources, Hauling for collecting and transporting existing loose material, and Construction for builder-owned gathering/staging plus work. These terms do not add or rename runtime work categories in 3.5B.

Milestones 3.4A, 3.4B and 3.4C are manually accepted. Milestone 3.4D is Implemented — Pending Manual Acceptance. Its global player-facing matrix lists active authoritative ant records whether or not their Colony View visual is loaded. Excavation, Construction and Hauling are the only functional columns because only those categories have real executors. Cells display mapped skills and edit the existing record-owned 1–4/Disabled values; developer diagnostics read the same values.

Changing a matrix value resets subsequent autonomous evaluation but never cancels an active job, changes a skill, pauses simulation or changes a developer autonomy override. Current activity and real failure/waiting text are displayed where the existing agent/job state exposes them. Surface Preparation, Foraging, Production, Combat and Brood Care stay out of the functional player matrix until real executors exist.

items.title: Required architecture boundaries
items.text:
• Job choice must not live in UI code.
  • Navigation calculates routes; it does not decide why an ant travels.
  • Work progress and physical resources remain authoritative outside visuals.
  • Cancellation and interruption must release reservations exactly once.
  • Construction preserves builder self-supply.
  • Hundreds-of-ants goals require controlled update rates and shared data, but do not justify DOTS/ECS before profiling.

items.title: Future cross-region work boundary
items.text: WV-A preserves the active job/order identity and valid partial work while an ant changes regions. A cross-view destination is region-scoped and composes a source-local route, one capacity-one entrance transaction and a destination-local route. The current Colony Vector2Int job targets and A* service remain unchanged; they are not valid Surface coordinates. An occupied or invalid entrance produces a recoverable waiting/failure state and releases reservations only through the owning job's existing cancellation rules. Autonomous cross-view selection and cost comparison are deferred to WV-D. See World View Foundation.

items.title: Not implemented
items.text: Excavation, personal inventory, explicit pickup, Material Storage, autonomous Soil/Stone hauling and functional Background construction are now real. Gathering, production, combat, brood care, forced-work orders, Draft Mode, group tactics, local avoidance, persistence, rooms and production-scale indexing require later milestones.

items.title: Ant Movement and Navigation
items.text:
Movement and navigation are the most extensively implemented and tested foundations in the project. They deliberately separate world truth, movement capability, route planning, and motor execution.

The established grip/support/falling rules describe the side-on underground Colony View. WV-B1 now also implements a separate top-down Surface navigator; the two local graphs and coordinate types are not interchangeable.

items.title: WV-B1 Surface-local movement
items.text:
SurfaceWorldData owns a bounded deterministic 64×64 obstacle grid, independently of ChunkedWorldData. SurfacePathfinder performs bounded deterministic A* over SurfaceCell: cardinal and diagonal steps are allowed, but a diagonal is rejected unless both adjacent cardinal cells are open. SurfaceNavigationMotor follows those cells kinematically from the shared simulation-clock delta, so pause freezes it and 1×/2×/3× remain compatible. It has no gravity, grip, excavation or falling states.

TwoViewWorldCoordinator accepts Surface pointer conversion only while World View is active. Colony orders are rejected for Surface residents, and Colony designation input is disabled in World View. Entrance travel asks only the source region's local motor to reach its typed approach cell; there is no autonomous cross-region pathfinder in WV-B1.

items.title: Authoritative rules
items.text:
• Every resident coordinate has one Background Tile and at most one foreground Solid Tile.
  • A blocking Solid prevents occupancy; excavation will remove only eligible foreground material.
  • Exposed natural Earth and Stone Backgrounds are grippable at normal speed.
  • Prepared Background grants the same access with a provisional 1.25x movement-speed multiplier.
  • Sky is non-grippable; without ground or grip an ant can fall.
  • Full-body clearance is separate from grip, grounding, traversability, and reachability.
  • Valid diagonal connections cannot cut blocked corners.
  • Stable movement follows shared navigation; Rigidbody2D gravity is reserved for Falling.

items.title: Production flow
items.text:
flowchart LR
  W[ChunkedWorldData] --> C[Clearance and capability]
  W --> M[Shared GridNavigationMap]
  C --> M
  M --> P[GridPathfinder and scheduler]
  P --> S[GridNavigationWorldService]
  S --> G[GridNavigationMotor]
  G --> V[Ant visual and status]

GridNavigationWorldService is the per-world owner of the shared map and bounded scheduler. GridNavigationMotor exposes the narrow destination, cancellation, and status boundary used by selection and survival interactions. The command layer does not implement a competing movement system.

Milestone 3.4B binds the service to the scene simulation clock. While paused, the scheduler consumes no request/node budget and fixed-step motors, climbing and Rigidbody2D falling do not run because Time.timeScale is zero. Pending requests and active routes remain owned and resume unchanged. The original fixedDeltaTime and maximumDeltaTime remain constant at 1×/2×/3× and are restored after the clock component is disabled or destroyed.

items.title: Known limitations
items.text:
• Friendly overlap is currently intentional; local avoidance and congestion behavior are future work.
  • The current grid is a deterministic authored development world, not procedural streaming gameplay.
  • General multiple-ant traffic, reservations, and deadlock handling are not complete gameplay systems.
  • The older AntSurfaceMotor and PlayerMovementInput course remains for regression testing. It is not the normal control model.
  • The original movement prototype still has pending ceiling, complete-corner-route, Auto Step-Over, and camera-follow completion work; that does not invalidate the accepted grid-navigation milestones.

items.title: Future World View navigation
items.text:
World View will use top-down surface movement over its own explicit coordinate and chunk space. It may use different local connections, obstacles and movement presentation from Colony View. The established underground grounded/gripping/climbing/falling rules remain valid in Colony View and must not be simplified to make both views use one local motor or path graph.

WV-A defines cross-view travel as:

  1. a Colony View route to a valid nest entrance;
  2. one controlled residency/representation transition; and
  3. a World View route from the paired surface entrance.

The same authoritative ant, inventory, needs, job and reservation state continues through all three stages. Only one live movement representation may own the ant at a time. The initial entrance has capacity one. A transaction reserves it, revalidates the destination and commits one residency revision idempotently; failure restores source residency. Local cost is simulated travel time, while future total cost adds an entrance wait/interaction estimate and destination-local travel. Autonomous composition remains deferred to WV-D.

Hidden loaded regions continue using the shared simulation clock. Future unloaded chunks require reduced-fidelity travel and job simulation rather than full physics or per-frame path execution. The reconciliation rules for an ant that returns to a loaded chunk must be deterministic and must not duplicate distance, work, resources or elapsed needs.

WV-B should introduce a separate SurfaceCell and Surface-local navigator. It must not pass a Surface coordinate to GridPathfinder, reuse Colony grip/falling edges for top-down movement or generalise GridNavigationMotor until a demonstrated shared abstraction exists. See World View Foundation.

items.title: Future acceptance
items.text:
Dynamic excavation and functional conversion must locally invalidate affected Colony View navigation data. Future Colony View agents must use the same route and motor rules; they cannot teleport, fly through unsupported space, or bypass clearance because a task system requested it. Future World View agents require equally explicit surface rules, while cross-view travel must pass through a valid entrance rather than bypassing either local navigation system.

Future diagram or screenshot: grid anchors, prepared-speed region, falling transition, and an invalidated route after terrain mutation.

items.title: Implemented identity model
items.text:
Each ant is represented by one authoritative plain-C# AntRecord. Stable AntId and ColonyId values, caste, attributes, lifecycle, skills, needs, work priorities and personal inventory belong to the record rather than to the visual GameObject. AntEntityBinding connects a runtime visual to an existing record, while a visual-claim registry prevents duplicate live representations.

The deterministic development ants are:

Name Caste Strength Agility Endurance Mara Queen 7 5 8 Pip Worker 4 8 5 Tala Worker 6 6 7

This identity and attribute foundation is complete and manually accepted. Visual destruction does not delete the record, and deceased records reject movement orders. Save/load and actual death gameplay are not implemented.

items.title: Implemented skill foundation
items.text:
Queen and Worker records share seven ordinary skills:

  • Excavation
  • Surface Preparation
  • Construction
  • Hauling
  • Foraging
  • Combat
  • Brood Care

All begin at level 0 and can reach level 100. A successful future activity can call the explicit learn-by-doing API; starting or cancelling work must not award experience.

items.title: Provisional progression
items.text:
• XP needed from level L to L+1: 100 + 5L.
  • Cumulative XP at level L: 100L + 2.5L(L-1).
  • Level 100 caps at 34,750 total XP.
  • After a provisional 24-hour inactivity grace period, skill value above 50 decays by 0.25 levels per inactive hour and stops at 50.
  • Needs and Rested modifiers can multiply a valid XP award without changing stored base progression rules.

These values are development placeholders. The foundation is implemented and automated-tested; its manual acceptance was recorded through the approved transition to milestone 3.2A.

items.title: Implemented personal inventory
items.text:
Each Queen or Worker record owns an independent stack-based inventory. Natural slot capacity is based only on current Hauling level: one slot at 0–19, two at 20–39, three at 40–59, four at 60–79 and five at 80–100. Soil and Stone provisionally stack to 10. Compatible additions merge before opening another slot; incompatible resources never share a slot.

If Hauling decay lowers capacity, occupied overflow remains intact and recoverable. New additions are blocked until occupied usage is within the reduced capacity. Inventory survives visual rebinding and selection changes. Equipment slots, weight, saddlebags and final balance are not implemented.

items.title: Planned individuality
items.text: The approved design expects equipment, permanent death, work efficiency from skills, and persistent individual histories. Roles will affect autonomous priorities rather than lock ants out of normal skills. Exact attribute formulas, equipment effects, ageing, and save serialization remain unresolved or unimplemented.

items.title: Boundaries
items.text:
• Skills never silently outrank player-assigned work priorities.
  • The current work-speed multiplier is exposed for future jobs and does not alter navigation speed.
  • The temporary ordered-work productivity bonus is approved in principle, but its value and implementation remain TBD.
  • A working founding queen is the intended start; older ordinary-ant-to-queen progression language is superseded.

See Food, Water and Survival for needs modifiers and Ant AI and Job Management for future priority selection.

items.title: Art Foundation
items.text: The custom Colony and World tilesets are preserved and prepared as separate candidate libraries. Milestone 3.5A additionally binds two reviewed full-cell Colony candidates through four existing visual Tile assets without changing gameplay authority.

items.title: Direction
items.text:
• Colony View uses warm soil, cool stone, dark excavated interiors and restrained green/root/fungus accents.
  • World View uses richer vegetation greens, warm soil/path browns, grey-blue water and natural prop accents.
  • Pixel edges stay crisp through Point filtering, no compression and no mipmaps.
  • Appearance never defines terrain behavior; gameplay material definitions remain authoritative.

Tools/Art/prepare_tilesets.py rebuilds them from manually reviewed rectangles recorded in Tools/Art/tileset_manifest.json; it does not assume a uniform 32-pixel source grid or stretch a crop to change its aspect ratio.

items.title: View boundaries
items.text:
Colony View remains side-on and retains one permanent Background plus an optional foreground Solid per resident cell. Many source candidates visually combine cavities, exposed edges and surrounding terrain, so they are not yet safe replacements for those independent layers.

World View remains approved future design only. Its regular top 7x10 terrain block is prepared as a separate library, while variable-size props remain source-only pending reviewed footprints and pivots. No World scene, navigation, transition or exploration system is added.

items.title: Limitations
items.text:
• Colony_R02_C01 now presents Soil/Natural Earth and Colony_R04_C01 presents Stone/Natural Stone; Background variants use darker Tile colours.
  • These mappings are reviewed full-cell textures but have not passed seamless-edge acceptance.
  • Rounded borders, dark gutters and coloured edge artefacts remain visible in places.
  • The one-time reduction from 1254x1254 source sheets to 32-pixel candidates loses fine detail.
  • Colony art still needs semantic layer separation; World props need individual extraction.
  • Wider production mapping and Colony/World Tile Palettes are deferred until visual and semantic review.

Automated preparation verification, Unity import validation and the strict documentation build pass. Visual, seamless-edge and gameplay-camera acceptance remain manual.

The full source analysis, future artwork needs and seven-step Unity inspection checklist are maintained in Documentation/ArtDirection.md.

items.title: Brood and Reproduction
items.text: Brood and reproduction are approved design, not implemented gameplay.

items.title: Founding sequence
items.text:
The intended first controllable ant is a working founding queen. The early colony sequence is:

  1. Excavate an accessible chamber.
  2. Construct at least three Nursery Background tiles.
  3. Explicitly authorise an initial brood of three larvae.
  4. Physically feed the larvae on multiple occasions.
  5. Allow surviving brood to mature into three individually controllable general-purpose workers.

This supersedes older plans in which an ordinary player ant later transformed into a queen.

items.title: Approved rules
items.text:
• Reproduction always requires explicit player authorisation; spare capacity alone cannot trigger it.
  • Each functional Nursery Background tile supplies exactly one brood slot.
  • Nursery function can operate without an enclosing room.
  • Proper enclosure may grant room-quality efficiency, but not extra base capacity.
  • Removing occupied nursery capacity pauses development rather than silently deleting brood.
  • Brood Care is one of the seven universal learn-by-doing skills.
  • Individual ant death is permanent once death gameplay exists.

items.title: Open decisions
items.text:
• Exact egg-to-larva-to-pupa-to-adult presentation and timing.
  • Feeding thresholds, resource types, and failure consequences.
  • Brood mortality and reassignment when capacity is removed.
  • Later brood sizes and queen work/reproduction trade-offs.
  • Colony behavior after queen death.

items.title: Dependencies
items.text:
Brood implementation depends on accepted excavation, resource-backed construction, Nursery conversion, physical food logistics, autonomous jobs, lifecycle transitions, and persistence. Those dependencies are not yet complete, so brood must not be introduced as an isolated shortcut.

See Colony Construction and Rooms, Food, Water and Survival, and Ant AI and Job Management.

items.title: Approved construction model
items.text:
Construction is physical, location-based work. Milestone 3.4A implements conversion of exposed Background cells after required materials are gathered and consumed. Recipes and balance remain provisional.

The ant performing construction must personally gather and deliver its own materials, including multiple trips. A separate hauler must not silently complete the builder's supply responsibility. Reservations prevent double allocation; cancelling construction leaves unused delivered or reserved materials physical and recoverable.

items.title: Functional Backgrounds
items.text:
Approved functions include:

  • Nursery
  • Sleeping
  • Food Storage
  • Water Storage
  • Material Storage
  • production functions still to be specified
  • burial

Each functional Background tile provides one unit of base capacity. Material Storage uses one tile per inventory slot and may later support optional filters. Function and locomotion remain separate properties: a functional tile can still be traversable and grippable.

Milestone 3.4A can construct Prepared, Nursery, Sleeping, Food Storage, Water Storage and Material Storage Background. Functional results expose one empty capacity unit; Nursery is capacity-only because brood remains excluded. Function, presentation and navigation refresh from the authoritative Background transaction.

items.title: Implemented builder workflow
items.text:
The selected conversion becomes a Construction job in the shared registry. Its reserved builder uses compatible carried material first, otherwise reserves the closest reachable compatible Material Storage or loose drop, collects into personal inventory, stages the material at the site and repeats if necessary. Timed work uses Construction skill and Rested modifiers. Completion consumes staged material exactly once and changes only the Background. Interruption preserves progress and physical ownership; designation cancellation exposes staged material as a recoverable loose drop.

If the builder lacks inventory capacity, it retains material needed by this construction job and unloads unnecessary stacks. It first reserves the closest reachable compatible Material Storage and travels there before depositing only enough to free capacity. With no reachable capacity, it creates a validated recoverable drop at its current anchor. The same construction order then resumes. Bounded failure and interruption release only pending reservations; they do not erase cargo, staged material, progress or job ownership.

Loose drops remain traversable and cannot by themselves prevent ordinary progression. Future clutter concentration may slow movement and loose resources may reduce cleanliness or quality in enclosed rooms, while stored material is excluded. Those thresholds and penalties are provisional and are not implemented in 3.4A.

Current provisional recipes cost one Soil for Prepared, Nursery, Sleeping, Food Storage or Material Storage, and one Stone for Water Storage. Base duration is four simulation hours.

Milestone 3.5A previews the selected recipe over a bounded hover/drag rectangle by calling the construction registry's non-mutating authoritative validation. Valid cells are green, invalid/occupied cells red and existing conversions muted with a separate symbol. Right-click in Background Conversion mode invokes the existing cancellation transaction for only that cell, so staged material still becomes a recoverable loose drop and no movement order leaks through.

items.title: Rooms and doors
items.text: The approved design allows mixed-use spaces. Enclosure is not required for base tile function, but an enclosed specialised room may earn quality or efficiency bonuses. Every opening into an enclosed room requires a door. Exact enclosure detection, door rules, scoring, mixed-use penalties, and quality formulas remain unresolved.

items.title: 2026-10-15 — Specify one-seed Surface and underground Colony generation
items.text:
• Approve one versioned world seed with independent deterministic Surface and Colony random domains; generation order and runtime timing cannot affect output.
  • Keep the initial Surface 64×64, predominantly Grass and approximately centre its one entrance.
  • Make the Colony entirely underground and predominantly solid Dirt/Soil. Put its exit on the approximately central topmost boundary and begin with exactly one minimum passage and small chamber containing the founding queen.
  • Preserve entrance.founding-nest.001, typed endpoints, capacity-one handoff, existing excavation/navigation authorities, rendering isolation and the Mara/Pip/Tala development fixture.
  • Keep terrain, extractable Solid material, finite source records, loose physical resources and entrance features separate.
  • Defer implementation to WV-B2B. 128×128 Colony bounds, exact chamber geometry, numerical weights, stable Surface/source IDs and PRNG/version details remain implementation approvals, not reopened product vision.

items.title: 2026-10-14 — Implement WV-B1 with a reversible loaded-representation adapter
items.text:
• Approve the proposed 64×64 Surface, (0,0) logical origin, one-unit cells, 32×32 future partition seam, fixed obstacles and no-corner-cut diagonal movement for WV-B1.
  • Keep both regions and one GameObject/binding per development ant loaded. A handoff switches the enabled local motor only after one guarded destination-region commit; failure restores the recorded source approach. This is a replaceable adapter for future unloading, not a change in authority.
  • Use two camera objects so position/zoom memory is independent by construction. Only the active camera and local pointer context are enabled; switching does not touch orders, residency or clock state.
  • Keep accepted Colony grip/falling unchanged and add no gravity to Surface movement. The WV-B1 prompt's conflicting broad gravity sentence does not supersede the approved WV-A local-navigation contract.
  • Defer every resource, natural-rest, foraging, extraction, autonomous cross-view, streaming, persistence and additional-entrance system.

items.title: 2026-10-14 — Specify the first two-view and founding-survival contract
items.text:
• Use distinct typed Colony and Surface coordinates under stable region identities; preserve the existing Colony integer-centre convention and local A* implementation.
  • Keep one authoritative ant record and one region residency. A capacity-one entrance transaction performs physical approach, exact-once residency commit and rollback-safe representation handoff.
  • Switch Colony/World cameras and input manually while preserving per-view camera state; switching never pauses, orders or teleports.
  • Keep both first regions loaded on the accepted clock. Cross-view autonomous jobs are WV-D and unloaded simulation is WV-F.
  • Use finite non-regenerating seed/freshwater sources for the first slice, direct consumption without storage, recoverable extraction output, a non-solid one-unit water payload/cache and safe natural rest.
  • Recommend, but do not yet approve, a 64×64 initial Surface, 32×32 candidate Surface chunks and natural rest at half the constructed recovery rate.

items.title: 2026-10-14 — Separate extraction output from collection and transport
items.text:
• Successful Soil/Stone excavation always creates physical loose output and never adds it directly to the excavator's inventory.
  • The excavated cell is the authoritative output location. Existing compatible same-cell stacks fill first, followed by at most one new bounded stack; an unrepresentable yield leaves the Solid intact.
  • Foraging discovers resources, Extraction removes them, Hauling collects and transports loose resources, and Construction retains builder-owned self-supply from inventory, storage or drops.
  • Excavation does not require storage, unload inventory or assign a hauling job. The accepted hauling scheduler and construction reservation/conservation rules remain unchanged.
  • This supersedes the 12 October excavation auto-pickup rule without changing stack limits, recipes or wider World View scope.

items.title: 2026-10-14 — Keep designation preview and first Colony art binding presentation-only
items.text:
• Excavation and construction registries expose non-mutating cell evaluation used by both preview and commit, preventing duplicated terrain/occupancy rules.
  • The command controller owns only a bounded transient preview and consumes compatible-tool right-click before normal context orders.
  • Existing cancellation APIs remain responsible for ownership, reservation and staged-material recovery.
  • Only Colony_R02_C01 (Soil/Earth) and Colony_R04_C01 (Stone) are allow-listed; Background variants are darker visual tints, all mapped Tiles are collider-free, and no seamless/autotile acceptance is implied.
  • Composite cavities, decorations, Prepared/functional Background art and World View runtime remain deferred.

This log summarises approved decisions. It does not approve unresolved details or replace the GDD.

items.title: Approved decisions

items.title: Adding an entry
items.text: Record only decisions explicitly approved by the user or already marked authoritative in the GDD. Include the date, the decision, and its implementation consequence. If a topic is unresolved, add it to Open decisions instead of silently choosing a default.

items.title: WV-B2A documentation gate
items.text:

items.title: Approved World View direction
items.text:
The WV-B1 World View foundation is implemented and awaiting its remaining broad regression/manual acceptance. It provides a bounded top-down Surface connected to side-on Colony View through one nest entrance. Persistent ants and the simulation clock are shared; switching views must not duplicate ants or stop the hidden region. WV-B2A specifies future generation but does not authorise WV-B2B runtime work.

The specified delivery order is:

  1. WV-A complete: approve two-view coordinate, residency, entrance, navigation and survival contracts as documentation;
  2. WV-B1: build one small bounded surface, manual view switching and one entrance transition;
  3. WV-C1: add finite-source discovery, direct survival and natural rest;
  4. WV-C2: add recoverable seed/water extraction, hauling and storage;
  5. WV-D: add bounded autonomous cross-view jobs;
  6. expand surface chunks and environments incrementally;
  7. WV-F: add lightweight unloaded-chunk simulation; and
  8. consider predators, rival colonies and wider ecology only through later approved scopes.

The authoritative prerequisites and phase boundaries are in Documentation/DevelopmentRoadmap.md.

items.text: Documentation maintenance is part of milestone completion. It is not a separate optional cleanup task.

items.title: Source hierarchy
items.text:
1. Inspect code, authored Unity content, and actual test output.
  2. Update Documentation/CurrentGameState.md with what is implemented and verified.
  3. Update Documentation/DevelopmentRoadmap.md with status, evidence, and the next authorised action.
  4. Update Documentation/GameDesignDocument.md only when the user approves a design change.

If evidence conflicts, record the discrepancy. Do not convert a plan into an implementation claim or an automated result into manual acceptance.

items.title: Generated underground contract
items.text:
WV-B2A approves an entirely underground Colony: no Sky row, above-ground layer or generated falling shaft. The recommended initial bounds are 128×128 cells in four-by-four existing 32×32 chunks. Every cell retains a permanent natural Background and initially has a Solid except the protected top-boundary entrance passage and exactly one starting chamber. Existing solid.soil is the provisional Dirt majority and solid.stone forms clustered deposits; excavation continues to create the existing physical Soil/Stone drops and invalidate local navigation.

Sand and Mud remain disabled until supported definitions, yields, art and tests are approved. Exact dimensions, weights and chamber geometry await WV-B2B approval. See Procedural World Generation.

items.title: Colony View two-layer world model
items.text:
The implemented terrain foundation belongs to the underground Colony View. Each cell in a resident 32×32 chunk contains exactly one permanent Background Material and zero or one foreground Solid Material. Missing chunks are unavailable rather than silently generated during a query.

The two layers have different responsibilities:

Layer Purpose Mutation rule Background Persistent substrate, grip, movement speed, and future colony function May be converted or prepared; never absent in a resident cell Foreground Solid Blocking/excavatable material and supporting geometry Removed only by a completed eligible excavation transaction

Visual Tilemaps and the collision-only Tilemap are projections of authoritative world data. The visual layers do not own gameplay state.

These Background/Solid semantics must be preserved for Colony View when World View is added. They are not automatically the terrain schema for the future top-down surface.

items.title: Implemented terrain foundations
items.text:
• Sparse signed-coordinate chunk data and explicit bounded generation.
  • Covered, Exposed, Supported, Unsupported, Unknown, and Unavailable classification.
  • Material definitions with independent movement-blocking and navigation-support flags.
  • Background and foreground Tilemap rendering.
  • A collision-only Tilemap with composite collider generation.
  • Whole-body rotated-capsule clearance queries.
  • Local refresh and navigation invalidation seams for controlled development mutations.
  • Natural Earth/Stone grip, Prepared speed, and non-grippable Sky behavior.

Milestone 3.3B connected these foundations to player designations and autonomous excavation work. Milestone 3.3C added personal inventory and explicit physical pickup/drop transfer; its historical automatic excavation pickup was superseded by Milestone 3.5B. Excavation now always leaves committed yield loose. Milestone 3.3D lets ants deliver those physical materials into filtered one-slot Material Storage Background tiles.

Milestone 3.4A adds player-designated Background conversion. Completion consumes builder-staged Soil/Stone, preserves foreground Solid occupancy, refreshes the Background Tilemap and invalidates local navigation through the existing mutation seam.

Milestone 3.4C exposes ordinary Colony View Excavate, six-recipe Build, and Cancel designation tools through the authored player HUD. Single-cell and bounded-drag input still delegates to the accepted registries. Cancellation retains the existing conserving material behavior, and uGUI/developer-IMGUI hit testing blocks designation start or release over interface panels.

Milestone 3.5A adds a read-only hover/drag preview. Excavation cells are amber when the excavation registry reports eligible, red when invalid and muted with an explicit marker when already designated. Background Conversion uses the same pattern with green valid cells and the selected recipe's authoritative construction validation. The preview does not create jobs or terrain objects and clears on tool exit, blocked pointer focus or pause.

Right-click in Excavation mode cancels only an excavation designation under the pointer; right-click in Background Conversion cancels only construction. The click is consumed even when the target is empty, preventing a movement order from dispatching through the tool. Select-mode contextual right-click and the existing Cancel tool remain unchanged.

items.title: Implemented excavation and material handling
items.text:
Excavate mode creates registry-owned jobs for eligible foreground Solid cells. Autonomous ants select them through the accepted priority/path-cost rules, reserve exclusively, reach a valid adjacent anchor and make incremental progress. Safe interruption retains progress. Completion removes only the foreground Solid and preserves the Background.

The stable job-keyed transaction preflights the complete loose output before terrain removal. The excavator's inventory and storage availability are deliberately irrelevant. Yield first merges into compatible partial stacks at the excavated authoritative cell, then may create one new bounded stack there. The logical drop model permits multiple traversable stacks on a cell, so this is always the preferred/current placement; no alternate-cell search is needed. A failed or unrepresentable output leaves the Solid intact, and retries cannot duplicate yield. Successful commit preserves Background, refreshes the affected visual/collision cell and invalidates local navigation.

Loose Soil and Stone stacks have stable identity, quantity, cell and provisional maximum stack 10. A selected ant can right-click a drop, reserve an eligible quantity, navigate adjacent and pick it up. Developer Only controls can drop a selected carried quantity at the ant's current valid anchor. Compatible same-cell stacks merge; failed or cancelled transfers preserve material and release reservations.

Foraging means discovering or identifying resources. Extraction means physically removing them and producing loose material. Hauling is the separate pickup/transport activity. Construction remains builder-owned self-supply from carried inventory, storage or loose drops. Excavation never assigns hauling automatically, and a no-storage colony simply retains recoverable loose output.

Material Storage remains physical rather than a global wallet. Each functional Background cell owns one compatible stack and incoming reservation. Autonomous haulers reserve source and destination, carry partial loads through personal inventory, and deposit only after reaching a valid adjacent anchor. Already-carried material produces an owner-only self-deposit task.

items.title: Surface Preparation
items.text: Preparation is now one 3.4A resource-backed Background conversion target. It costs a provisional one Soil and four simulation work hours. It does not unlock natural climbing: intact exposed Earth and Stone are already grippable. Prepared Background retains the provisional 1.25x travel-speed benefit. Final balance remains unresolved.

items.title: Future World View terrain
items.text:
Historical WV-A direction; WV-B1 now implements the bounded foundation. World View is top-down with distinct typed Surface coordinates, a deterministic bounded first region and a Surface-local terrain/navigation authority. WV-B1 fixed the development dimensions, cell scale, future partition seam, obstacle/diagonal rules and authored composition. WV-B2A now specifies the generated terrain contract; Surface mutation and expansion remain future work.

The first surface slice must be a small playable area around a known nest entrance. It should prove surface presentation, traversal, a narrow collection/return loop and persistent state before additional chunks or environments are introduced. Read-only queries must not generate missing surface chunks or treat unloaded space as empty, matching the existing conservative availability rule without requiring both views to share the same tile layers.

The first stable EntranceId maps one typed Colony endpoint to one typed Surface endpoint and has transition capacity one. Endpoint blockage invalidates approach/arrival and leaves the ant source-resident. Entrance construction, relocation, multiple entrances and terrain changes that would remove an endpoint remain deferred beyond the first slice.

items.title: Not implemented
items.text:
• Procedural generation runtime, durable chunk streaming, or save/load. WV-B2A specifies future generation but does not implement it.
  • World View surface terrain, nest-entrance transitions and cross-view terrain persistence.
  • Resource crafting, demolition, rooms and door construction.

See World View Foundation, Ant Movement and Navigation and Colony Construction and Rooms.

items.title: Accepted needs foundation
items.text: Milestone 3.2A is complete and manually accepted. Every authoritative ant record owns Health, Hunger, Thirst, Fatigue, and Rested qualification. State persists through selection changes and visual rebinding, and a deterministic development-world rebuild resets it.

items.title: Provisional values
items.text:
Rule Development value Starting Health / Hunger / Thirst 100 / 100 / 100 Starting Fatigue 20 Awake Hunger loss 1 per simulation hour Awake Thirst loss 1.4 per simulation hour Awake Fatigue gain 1.4 per simulation hour Rest recovery 16 Fatigue per simulation hour Critical Hunger threshold 10 or lower Critical Hunger damage 2 Health per simulation hour Critical Thirst effect Blocks ordinary skill XP Rested qualification Completed rest at Fatigue 20 or lower Maximum Rested work speed 1.15x Maximum Rested skill XP 1.25x Rested fade Returns to 1.0x by Fatigue 80

The work multiplier is exposed for future jobs and does not alter navigation speed. Zero Health pauses ordinary survival advancement but does not yet create death or corpse gameplay.

items.title: Physical interactions and autonomy
items.text:
Milestone 3.2B physical Eat, Drink, and Rest interactions and Milestone 3.2C autonomous survival are complete:

  • Food and water quantities belong to specific functional Background cells.
  • Resource and sleeping reservations belong to stable ant identities.
  • The ant chooses the lowest-cost reachable adjacent anchor through the shared grid pathfinder.
  • Arrival revalidates location and function before interaction.
  • Cancellation, replacement, failure, inactive/deceased state, and world reset release reservations.
  • Changing selection does not cancel another ant's valid order.
  • Autonomous ants seek Hunger/Thirst at 50 or below and Rest at Fatigue 60 or above.
  • Critical Thirst, Hunger, and Fatigue use deterministic precedence and may safely interrupt work/player orders only after a viable physical target is confirmed.
  • Ordinary needs use normalized urgency and hysteresis, and do not interrupt active colony work.
  • Failed searches use bounded retry backoff rather than per-frame path requests.

Eat reserves and consumes one resource.food.development unit after 0.5 simulation hour and restores 40 Hunger. Drink consumes one resource.water.development unit after 0.5 simulation hour and restores 50 Thirst. Rest recovers Fatigue over time and completes at the accepted Rested threshold. Interaction time advances at one simulation hour per real-time second in the development scene.

Milestone 3.4B routes needs, interactions, autonomous evaluation and retry/backoff through the authoritative simulation clock. Pause advances none of them and preserves any existing survival reservation. Running 1×/2×/3× changes simulated time per real second without changing the provisional per-simulation-hour rates above.

items.text: The WV-A specification adds design only, not runtime behavior: finite Surface seed and freshwater sources, direct eating/drinking without storage, extraction to recoverable output, one-unit non-solid water payloads, and safe natural rest. items.title: Not implemented
items.text:
Natural source discovery, seed/water extraction, food parcels, water caches, survival-supply hauling, cooking, food varieties, spoilage, water production, containers, death, corpses, and save/load remain outside the current slice. General ant inventory, Soil/Stone hauling, Material Storage and constructed survival fixtures do exist; they do not yet transport natural survival supplies.

See World View Foundation and Development Roadmap before extending this system.

items.title: Game Overview
items.text:
Milestone 3.5B is Implemented — Pending Manual Acceptance; 3.5A remains separately pending visual acceptance. Excavation now always leaves physical Soil/Stone output loose at the excavated cell, independent of the worker's inventory and storage. Hauling performs later pickup/transport, while builders may collect those drops directly. The development game opens paused at Day 1 08:00 with an authored uGUI player HUD and a global Work screen where priorities for active colony ants can be inspected and changed. Developer IMGUI starts hidden and remains deliberately accessible through F12 without replacing the player interface.

Accepted Milestone 3.4A permits player-designated conversion of exposed Background into Prepared, Nursery, Sleeping, Food Storage, Water Storage or Material Storage tiles. A Construction-priority ant personally supplies physical Soil/Stone, stages it at the site and performs timed work. Doors, rooms, brood and production remain future work.

items.title: Vision
items.text:
Ant Colony is a single-player, scrollable and zoomable 2D colony simulation with two interconnected perspectives. Colony View is the existing side-on underground space for excavation, construction, storage, brood and colony activity. World View is an approved but unimplemented top-down surface space for exploration, foraging, resource collection and later environmental threats. The intended world is persistent and chunk-based, while individual ants remain authoritative across both views.

The game should remain small enough to finish. Depth comes from physical work, individual needs and skills, shared terrain rules, and colony logistics rather than from a large collection of disconnected systems.

items.title: Player fantasy
items.text: The player guides a founding queen and, later, a growing colony through excavation, survival, construction, brood care, and defence. Ants are individuals rather than anonymous counters: each retains identity, attributes, learned skills, health, hunger, thirst, fatigue, equipment, and lifecycle state as the relevant systems are implemented.

items.title: Intended core loop
items.text:
1. Explore and understand the local underground space.
  2. Excavate accessible foreground material without removing the permanent Background.
  3. Convert exposed Background cells into useful colony functions using physical resources.
  4. Secure food, water, sleeping capacity, and nursery capacity.
  5. Authorise brood and support it until new workers mature.
  6. Assign work through colony priorities or temporary explicit orders.
  7. Expand while maintaining individual survival and preparing for hostile encounters.
  8. Travel through nest entrances to explore a small nearby surface, collect useful resources and return to the colony.

Only the foundations of this loop exist today. See Gameplay Mechanics for the system-by-system status.

The documentation-only WV-A contract now defines how the two views will connect without claiming implementation: distinct region coordinates, one persistent ant residency, a capacity-one entrance transaction, manual remembered cameras, a shared clock, finite nearby seed/freshwater, recoverable one-unit water carriage and natural rest. See World View Foundation.

items.title: Current playable development state
items.text:
The integrated AntGameDevelopment.unity scene is a deterministic development environment, not a finished game loop. It currently demonstrates:

  • authoritative two-layer world data and Tilemap projection;
  • whole-body clearance, Background grip, gravity, and grid navigation;
  • three selectable ants with persistent identity, attributes, skills, needs, priorities, and personal inventories;
  • a global work-priority matrix over authoritative ant records, including records without a loaded Colony View visual;
  • independent movement orders through the production grid motor;

items.title: Control model
items.text:
The approved player-facing model has three states:

  • Autonomous: an ant selects work and survival behavior from allowed priorities when those systems exist.
  • Temporary explicit order: the player requests a specific task. Completion, cancellation, or invalidation returns the ant to autonomy.
  • Draft Mode: a future persistent tactical state for move, attack, hold, defend-area, retreat, and group control.

Current implementation supports selection plus temporary Move, Eat, Drink, Rest and material Pickup orders, along with autonomous survival, colony work selection and autonomous hauling. It does not yet implement explicit forced-work orders or Draft Mode. The old WASD PlayerMovementInput path is retained strictly as a developer movement regression tool.

The accepted 3.4C player HUD provides roster selection, shared ant inspection, the global simulation clock, physical-resource ownership, readable job state and Colony View Select/Excavate/Build/Cancel tools without opening Developer Mode. WV-B1 adds a small development view/entrance strip, hides Colony commands in World View and provides Surface selection/right-click movement. It does not add Surface resources, cross-view jobs, alerts or Draft Mode.

items.title: Physical-world principles
items.text:
• Terrain, resources, capacity, and work should exist at world locations rather than as unexplained global counters.
  • Extraction always produces loose physical output; pickup and transport are separate Hauling actions.
  • Ants must navigate to a valid adjacent interaction position before acting.
  • The constructing ant is responsible for gathering and delivering its own materials, including multiple trips.
  • Valid partial work survives safe interruptions.
  • Reservations prevent duplicate consumption and must be released on cancellation or failure.

The current systems prove these principles through location-owned food/water, sleeping reservations, real excavation, per-ant inventory, reserved loose-drop pickup and cell-owned Material Storage. Material remains in exactly one authoritative inventory, world drop or storage stack; no global resource wallet exists.

Future natural sources preserve the same conservation rule. Direct consumption reserves and decrements a source exactly once without creating cargo. Extraction creates recoverable physical output before source quantity commits. Water uses a stable one-unit liquid payload/cache rather than an ordinary Soil/Stone drop. See World View Foundation.

items.title: Progression and failure
items.text: Skills improve through successful work. Hunger, thirst, fatigue, and health create survival pressure. Individual ant death is intended to be permanent, but actual death and corpse gameplay are not implemented. The colony outcome after queen death remains unresolved.

items.title: Approved world shape
items.text:
• One seed deterministically produces a top-down Surface and side-on underground Colony.
  • The initial Surface remains 64×64, predominantly Grass, with an entrance near (32,32).
  • The recommended initial Colony is 128×128, predominantly existing solid.soil, with Stone deposits and no Sky/above-ground row.
  • The Colony exit is on the topmost underground boundary. One minimum passage leads to exactly one small starting chamber containing the founding queen.
  • Terrain, finite source records, loose physical items and the entrance remain separate authorities.

The 128×128 Colony, 7×5 chamber, three-cell passage and exact generation weights are implementation recommendations awaiting WV-B2B approval.

items.title: Determinism contract
items.text:
Generation is identified by world seed, generation version, configuration ID and configuration revision. A frozen project-owned integer PRNG and stable hash derive named Surface, Colony, entrance and guarantee domains. Generation order, frame rate, camera state, dictionary order and ant movement cannot affect output.

Generation builds temporary data, applies protected entrance/chamber masks, places source records, validates the complete result and only then publishes it. Validation never rerolls a failed seed. Once published, excavation and depletion mutate the in-memory world; switching views never regenerates it.

items.title: Existing integration seams
items.text:
ChunkedWorldData, WorldTileCoordinates, the material registry, shared Colony navigation and excavation remain Colony authorities. SurfaceWorldData and SurfacePathfinder remain separate Surface authorities. Typed region locations, AntRegionResidencyRegistry, entrance.founding-nest.001 and the WV-B1 capacity-one transaction are preserved. TwoViewWorldCoordinator binds a completed scenario but does not own random generation, simulation or persistence.

The current SampleWorldGenerator remains a deterministic development fixture builder. The Mara/Pip/Tala scenario and its authored survival, storage and job fixtures stay available separately from the generated founding-colony scenario.

items.title: Terrain and sources
items.text:
Provisional, unapproved example weights are 82 Grass / 8 Water / 6 Stone ground / 4 obstacle on the Surface and 88 Soil / 12 Stone underground. Correlated noise, deterministic region growth and bounded clusters avoid uniform speckle. Sand and Mud remain disabled because the current project has no supported production definitions or yield contracts for them.

At least one finite food source and freshwater access/source must be reachable near the Surface entrance without constructed infrastructure. Sources are records on compatible terrain, not replacement terrain or loose drops. Exact types, quantities and balance belong to a later approved resource slice.

items.title: Validation gate
items.text: Before runtime publication, validate unique linked endpoints, protected clear approaches, one connected starting chamber, a clear/reachable queen spawn, reachable early sources, registered IDs, compatible terrain/source placement, valid chunk ownership, bounds and Grass/Dirt predominance. Deterministic bounded repairs may restore protected masks or relocate guarantee sources; structural or configuration failures reject the original seed with diagnostics.

items.title: WV-B2B boundary
items.text:
The smallest future implementation is a pure bounded builder/validator plus an explicit scenario selector and adapters into existing world authorities. It does not include source consumption, extraction, hauling, foraging, persistence, streaming, unloaded simulation, extra entrances or autonomous cross-view routes.

items.title: WV-B2A generation boundary — 15 October 2026
items.text:
The future generator is a pure initial-data producer, not a new runtime owner. It derives independent named Surface/Colony streams from one versioned world seed, builds temporary region/source/feature records, validates the complete cross-region result and only then publishes it. ChunkedWorldData plus existing material, navigation and excavation services remain Colony authorities; SurfaceWorldData/SurfacePathfinder remain separate Surface authorities. AntRegistry, residency, the clock, HUD, cameras and rendering are consumers, never generator dependencies. See Procedural World Generation.

The current development SampleWorldGenerator remains a fixture builder and is not the production generator. An explicit scenario/provider selection will keep Mara/Pip/Tala separate from the one-queen generated scenario. View switching and presentation rebuilds may not invoke generation or reset mutable world state.

items.title: WV-B1 implemented two-view boundary — 14 October 2026
items.text:
WV-B1 implements the typed and transactional subset of WV-A. AntColony.World owns region/cell value types plus bounded Surface data/A*; AntColony.Navigation owns the clock-driven kinematic Surface motor; AntColony.Commands owns exactly-one residency and the capacity-one entrance transaction; AntColony.Development composes both loaded regions, two cameras and explicit input contexts. AntRecord, AntRegistry, AntEntityBinding, the Colony world/navigation stack and SimulationClockController remain the existing authorities.

The development adapter keeps the same bound GameObject across regions and switches local motors after residency commit. This is intentionally reversible and prevents a second live binding; it does not make the visual authoritative. Surface activation failure restores source residency and pose. No second clock, generic coordinate conversion, cross-region A*, resource authority or streaming system was introduced.

This historical WV-A decision specified but did not itself implement one paired, pre-authored bidirectional entrance with capacity one ant; manual Colony/World presentation switching; physical approach and atomic residency/representation handoff; one shared clock; finite nearby sources; provisional liquid carriage; and natural rest.
