items.text: AntColony.Ants owns stable identity, colony membership, caste, attributes, lifecycle, skills, needs, per-ant work priorities and stack-based personal inventory. Runtime visuals bind to records rather than becoming the source of truth.

items.title: World data
items.text:
AntColony.World owns chunks, Background/Solid material definitions, loose material drops, physical Material Storage slots, the atomic excavation commit, classification, clearance, capability, pathfinding data, and scheduling. Visual and collision Tilemaps project that data through AntColony.WorldPresentation; they do not own stored quantities.

Milestone 3.5B narrows the atomic excavation boundary to terrain plus loose output. It validates the Solid and preflights the entire definition yield in WorldMaterialDropRegistry before removing foreground, then commits the prepared same-cell merge/new-stack result under the stable job key. AntInventory is not a destination or prerequisite of extraction. Pickup, autonomous storage hauling and construction self-supply continue through their existing independent reservation/transfer operations.

items.title: Art assets and presentation boundary
items.text:
Custom art is organised under Assets/_AntGame/Art/Colony and Assets/_AntGame/Art/World, with preserved originals separated from prepared candidate sprites. Tools/Art/prepare_tilesets.py records measured extraction rectangles and generates deterministic 32-pixel libraries; the resulting sprite names describe source position only.

Candidate sprites do not own or imply material identity. Colony art must be separated into Background, optional foreground Solid, exposed-edge and decoration responsibilities before binding to the existing Tilemap projection. Collision stays on the dedicated collision Tilemap. World art remains an unbound future-view library until its terrain and coordinate authority are approved.

Milestone 3.5A binds only reviewed Colony_R02_C01 for Soil, Colony_R05_C05 for Stone Solid and Colony_R05_C03 for Natural Stone Background. Darker Tile colours distinguish natural Background projections. Tile colliders remain None; the dedicated collision Tilemap continues to read only authoritative Solid definitions.

items.title: Navigation
items.text: One GridNavigationWorldService owns the shared navigation map and bounded scheduler for a world. Each GridNavigationMotor owns only its agent request and execution state. Command and interaction systems call the narrow motor API.

items.title: Commands and interactions
items.text:
AntColony.Commands handles selection, designation input, context orders, visual bindings, physical survival, synthetic work, real excavation, explicit material pickup/drop, autonomous hauling and real Background construction. Location-owned supplies remain in SurvivalInteractionWorld; job identity, ownership and progress remain in ColonyJobRegistry; designation registries are typed views over those same jobs rather than second queues. Source reservations remain in the world-drop or Material Storage authority, and carried stacks remain on the ant record. All travel reuses the shared map and motor.

ConstructionJobOrder reserves one builder and moves existing physical material through inventory into a cell-owned ConstructionSite. ConstructionWorldTransaction validates occupancy, source Background and staged quantity before consuming once, replacing only the Background, registering one functional-capacity slot, refreshing presentation and invalidating navigation.

When construction needs inventory capacity, InventoryCapacityRecoveryOperation is a reusable task-executor helper rather than a new hauling job. It protects the current task's resource type, uses existing path measurement and incoming storage reservations, commits deposits only after travel, or invokes the existing conserving drop transaction at a valid anchor. Cancellation releases uncommitted capacity reservations while leaving every physical quantity at its current owner. Loose drops remain ordinary traversable world data; future clutter penalties do not yet participate in navigation or room-quality calculation.

items.title: Development composition
items.text:
AntGameDevelopmentWorldHost assembles the deterministic integrated test world. It is a focused authored coordinator, not a global production manager. Developer controls and diagnostics expose authoritative state for acceptance checks.

SimulationClockController is the scene-owned runtime time authority. It starts at Day 1 08:00 paused, exposes read-only elapsed seconds/hours/day-time, and supplies bounded simulation deltas at 1×/2×/3×. Unity Time.timeScale stops fixed-step physics; the original timeScale, fixedDeltaTime and maximumDeltaTime are captured and restored. Fixed and maximum deltas stay at their project baselines, so faster speeds produce more fixed steps per real second rather than changing the physics step size. Each unscaled frame contribution is capped by maximumDeltaTime to avoid unbounded catch-up.

GameplayModeCoordinator owns only normal-gameplay policy: survival, colony work and hauling follow one enabled bundle unless Developer Mode forces a subsystem on or off. It never owns orders and never changes clock state. GridNavigationWorldService and the command controller use explicit clock references to stop scheduler and gameplay progress while paused. Camera movement remains intentionally unscaled.

Milestone 3.4C adds AntColony.PlayerUI as a presentation-only assembly. The authored PlayerHud.prefab contains focused roster, selected-ant inspector, simulation-control, Colony View command, physical-resource and job-status presenters. AntGameDevelopmentWorldHost binds them to the existing AntRegistry, command/designation registries, physical storage/drop/site owners and the single SimulationClockController; the HUD creates none of those authorities. Shared identity, needs, skills, inventory and job information is displayed independently from the inspector's separate Colony View position/navigation section.

The roster reads authoritative records and uses a narrow compatibility adapter to select a currently loaded SelectableGridAnt. It never defines identity from the GameObject and performs no repeated scene-wide discovery. This leaves future unloaded or World View records representable without inventing residency state now. The resource summary performs a bounded unscaled refresh and reports stored, carried, loose and staged ownership separately; reservations are not counted again because ownership does not change until commit.

AntSelectionCommandController retains accepted command and developer-IMGUI behavior, but no longer acts as the player HUD. It starts Developer Mode hidden and opens through F12 or the separate centre-top reopen control. DevelopmentWorldInspector still owns World/Debug developer panels and all seven categories remain available. The controller accepts only an IPlayerUiInputBlocker read-only hit test; the uGUI implementation uses the one EventSystem and GraphicRaycaster, while existing IMGUI rectangles protect developer controls. Selection, context orders, designation drag start/release and camera mouse input all consult the combined boundary. The temporary SimulationTimeControlStrip is no longer authored in the development scene.

The command toolbar declares only PlayerViewContext.Colony. Its Select, Excavate, Background conversion and cancellation actions delegate to accepted APIs. Area cancellation invokes construction and excavation registries, so staged construction material follows the existing recoverable-drop transaction. No view manager, World View state, surface input or shared world-coordinate abstraction was added.

Milestone 3.5A keeps preview state presentation-only inside AntSelectionCommandController. Each hovered or bounded drag cell is classified by the same excavation/construction registry validation used by commit. IMGUI draws the bounded overlay without per-cell GameObjects. Active-tool right-click is consumed before contextual orders and delegates to only the compatible registry cancellation API.

Milestone 3.4D adds a global ColonyManagementView and reusable authored work-priority row. The view enumerates active AntRecord entries and writes their existing AntWorkPrioritySet through a narrow command API that also schedules the next ordinary work evaluation. It does not select the ant, require a loaded visual, cancel active work or own job-choice logic. Rows may consult a loaded SelectableGridAnt only for current activity text. The player matrix exposes only Excavation, Construction and Hauling because those categories have real executors; developer diagnostics retain the full catalog over the same underlying values.

The management overlay remains inside the existing Canvas and EventSystem. Its full-screen raycast target protects priority clicks and scrolling from world/camera input. An optional keyboard-focus boundary consumes Escape for the modal before Colony View designation cancellation, without coupling command logic to uGUI types. Opening the overlay never owns or changes simulation-clock state.

items.title: Approved two-view target architecture
items.text:
Design boundary — not implemented. The responsibilities below describe constraints for future milestones. They deliberately avoid committing to final component or class names. Current runtime ownership above remains the implemented architecture.

flowchart LR
  A[Shared persistent ant and job state]
  C[Colony View region]
  W[World View region]
  E[Nest entrance transition]
  CC[Colony coordinates and local navigation]
  WC[Surface coordinates, chunks and local navigation]
  P[Active presentation and input context]
  L[Lightweight unloaded-region simulation]

  A --> C
  A --> W
  C --> CC
  W --> WC
  C <--> E <--> W
  P --> C
  P --> W
  A --> L

items.title: Responsibility boundaries
items.text: Concern Proposed responsibility Required invariant View management Select the presented region, camera and input context Switching views does not pause, clone or reinitialise the simulation Shared ant state Own identity, stats, skills, needs, inventory, lifecycle and job state independently of a view One authoritative ant record exists across all regions Region residency Record which region/chunk currently contains an ant and whether it has a loaded visual representation An ant cannot be resident in two regions or own two live representations simultaneously Coordinate spaces Keep Colony View cells, World View surface coordinates and entrance mappings explicit Coordinates from one view are never interpreted implicitly as coordinates in the other World chunks Own bounded surface data, loading, persistence and generation separately from Colony View's underground tile semantics Missing/unloaded chunks are unavailable, not assumed empty or generated by read-only queries Local navigation Let each view use navigation appropriate to its geometry and movement rules Colony gripping/falling remains intact; World View does not require the same local graph Cross-view navigation Compose local travel, an entrance transition and destination-region travel Cross-view jobs use one ant/order identity and expose recoverable transition failure states Transition boundary Validate source entrance, destination entrance, residency and representation handoff as one controlled operation Departure and arrival cannot duplicate or lose the ant or its inventory Simulation persistence Advance both views from the shared simulation clock whether or not they are presented View switching cannot freeze the hidden region or grant extra elapsed time Unloaded simulation Eventually advance important state with bounded reduced fidelity and reconcile it on reload No claim of full Rigidbody or frame-by-frame navigation outside loaded chunks

items.title: Coordinate and chunk policy
items.text:
Colony View retains its implemented signed cell/chunk coordinates and permanent Background plus optional Solid model. World View requires its own approved surface coordinate and terrain specification. A shared chunk size or data schema is not assumed merely because both regions are chunked. Cross-view references use stable region and entrance identities plus explicit local positions rather than one ambiguous global Vector2.

WV-A requires distinct ColonyCell and SurfaceCell value types wrapped by region-scoped location variants. The existing integer-centre Colony mapping is unchanged. WV-B1 approved and implemented a 64×64 logical Surface with a 32×32 future partition seam, one-unit cells and fixed obstacle/no-corner-cut rules. It still does not reuse ChunkedWorldData by assumption. WV-B2A specifies how a future generated Surface preserves that separation.

The first World View implementation should load one small bounded surface region around a known entrance. Continuous-world streaming, additional environments and distant chunks follow only after the bounded transition and return loop is validated.

items.title: Navigation and transitions
items.text:
A cross-view route is conceptually three parts: a local route to a nest entrance, a validated region transition, and a local route from the paired entrance. The local navigation implementations may differ, but job selection and order execution need a common way to report reachability, progress, cancellation and failure. Reservations associated with an ant or physical item must remain stable through the handoff or be released by explicit existing cancellation semantics.

The transition reserves the capacity-one entrance, completes the source local approach, revalidates both endpoints, acquires an idempotent commit guard, changes one residency revision and then performs a single representation handoff. Destination activation failure rolls residency back to the source; source ownership remains authoritative even if its visual must be restored later. Shared identity, needs, skills, jobs and inventory are never copied. Exact animation and timing remain WV-B approvals.

items.title: Simulation and persistence boundary
items.text:
• Both initial regions remain loaded and advance full simulation from the one SimulationClockController, including when hidden.
  • Pause freezes both regions, transition commits, route scheduling, needs, jobs, interactions and retry time. View switching never changes clock state.
  • Region residency is persistent authoritative state keyed by AntId; representation and camera state do not define it.
  • Save/version structure, durable Surface mutations and in-progress route persistence remain unapproved.
  • Reduced-fidelity unloaded simulation and reconciliation are explicitly deferred to WV-F; WV-B and WV-C must not simulate unloaded chunks.

items.title: Scene flow
items.text:
Scene Purpose Status AntMovementPrototype.unity Continuous-input surface movement regression course Retained developer fixture AntNavigationPrototype.unity Navigation classification and visualisation fixture Retained developer fixture AntGameDevelopment.unity Integrated world, ants, selection, movement, survival, jobs, excavation, inventory, storage, hauling and Background construction Primary development scene

There is no finished menu-to-game flow, Bootstrap scene, save selection, or production world-loading sequence yet. Future work must preserve the existing authored coordinator seams rather than introducing an unnecessary global manager.

No World View scene, surface region, view manager or transition runtime exists yet. Whether the two views ultimately use separate scenes, additive scenes or another authored composition is intentionally unresolved; future implementation must satisfy the ownership invariants above before choosing that packaging.

items.title: Test strategy
items.text:
• Plain-C# Edit Mode tests cover deterministic records, world rules, pathfinding, scheduling, and interactions.
  • Physics-backed tests cover collider projection, movement, falling, and integration behavior.
  • Play Mode tests cover scene wiring and end-to-end interaction slices.
  • Structural validators inspect authored scenes and prefabs.
  • Manual checklists cover visuals, input, timing, diagnostics, and behaviors that automation does not observe.
  • Focused development-UI tests cover exclusive category state, collapse/hide behavior, resolution bounds and shared pointer blocking before the complete regressions run.

Compilation, automated tests, and manual acceptance are recorded separately. A successful build never implies Unity Play Mode acceptance.

items.title: Architectural guardrails
items.text:
• Keep input/commands, task choice, navigation, motor execution, physics, and presentation separate.
  • Preserve Unity .meta files and serialized references.
  • Use Unity-aware null checks (component == null) for destroyed objects.
  • Prefer local invalidation and shared maps over per-ant world duplication.
  • Add major dependencies only after an identified need and explicit approval.

See the Documentation Workflow for keeping this page synchronized.

items.title: WV-B2A generated-world extension
items.text: The approved future generated-world contract is summarized in Procedural World Generation. One seed produces both regions without changing WV-B1 typed locations or entrance semantics. The Surface remains 64×64 and predominantly Grass. The Colony is entirely underground, predominantly solid Soil/Dirt and begins with one small chamber containing the founding queen beneath the top-boundary exit. Runtime implementation has not started, and the Mara/Pip/Tala fixture remains intact.

items.title: Status
items.text:
WV-B1 implemented; validation remains incomplete. Focused Edit/Play and complete Play suites pass, while complete graphics-capable Edit regression and manual acceptance remain outstanding. The authoritative detailed contract is Documentation/WorldViewTechnicalSpecification.md. Runtime now covers typed regions/residency, one bounded Surface, manual cameras, Surface-local movement and one entrance. Natural resources, rest, extraction, autonomous cross-view routing, streaming and unloaded simulation remain deferred.

The accepted foundation is one bounded top-down Surface region, one pre-authored bidirectional entrance with capacity one, manual remembered Colony/World cameras, physical ant approach travel, finite nearby seed/freshwater, one-unit recoverable liquid carriage and safe natural rest. Both starting regions remain loaded on the one simulation clock.

items.title: Existing integration seams
items.text:
• AntRecord and AntRegistry remain the single source for identity, needs, skills, inventory and lifecycle.
  • AntEntityBindingRegistry already prevents duplicate live visuals and is the core representation-handoff guard.
  • SimulationClockController remains the only clock; GameplayModeCoordinator stays independent from view choice.
  • Existing grid navigation remains the Colony-local implementation. World View receives its own top-down coordinate and navigator.
  • Current job/resource systems provide stable identity, reservation, exact-once commit and cancellation patterns, but their unscoped Vector2Int locations are Colony-only.
  • PlayerHudController is presentation-only and can gain a narrow view selector without owning simulation.
  • AntGameDevelopmentWorldHost and Mara/Pip/Tala remain untouched regression content.

WV-B1 adds AntRegionResidencyRegistry, SurfaceWorldData, SurfacePathfinder, SurfaceNavigationMotor, NestEntranceTransitionService and TwoViewWorldCoordinator. It still has no natural source, liquid payload, cross-view route planner or unloaded-region model.

items.title: Implemented WV-B1 fixture and controls
items.text:
• Surface bounds are 64×64 logical cells from (0,0) through (63,63) with a future-only 32×32 partition size.
  • Fixed obstacle rectangles provide alternate deterministic routes. Diagonals require both adjacent cardinal cells to be traversable.
  • Colony View and World View select one camera/input context while both regions remain loaded. Each camera object retains its own position and zoom.
  • In World View, left-click selects a Surface-resident ant and right-click orders a valid Surface cell. Colony designation tools are hidden and their pointer conversion is disabled.
  • Use Nest Entrance reserves entrance.founding-nest.001 for the selected ant. Each local motor reaches its typed approach before residency can commit.
  • The implementation preserves one existing bound GameObject and switches its active local motor during handoff. Residency and binding identity remain authoritative; activation failure rolls back to the source.

Focused Unity verification passed 8/8 Edit Mode and 2/2 Play Mode; complete Play Mode passed 69/69. The manual checklist remains in Documentation/CurrentGameState.md.

items.title: Regions, residency and entrance
items.text:
flowchart LR
  A[AntRecord and one AntResidency]
  C[Colony region<br/>ColonyCell + existing A*]
  E[EntranceId<br/>capacity one]
  W[Surface region<br/>SurfaceCell + top-down navigation]
  VC[Colony camera/input]
  VW[World camera/input]

  A --> C
  A --> W
  C <-->|typed Colony endpoint| E
  E <-->|typed Surface endpoint| W
  VC -. presents .-> C
  VW -. presents .-> W

ColonyCell and SurfaceCell are different value types beneath a region-scoped location union. They never convert implicitly. Colony integer coordinates remain Unity cell centres. An entrance stores both endpoints explicitly; there is no arithmetic conversion between views.

Residency is authoritative state keyed by AntId: one region, one typed location and one revision. A GameObject is only a loaded projection. The selected ant is retained by ID; if it is outside the active view, the shared inspector remains available and reports Not in current view, while local world orders are unavailable.

items.title: Safe transition
items.text:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Requested
  Requested --> Approaching: capacity and source route accepted
  Requested --> Rejected: validation fails
  Approaching --> Ready: source anchor reached
  Approaching --> Cancelled: route/order cancelled
  Ready --> Committing: running clock and one-shot guard
  Committing --> Arrived: one residency revision and destination binding
  Committing --> RolledBack: destination activation failed
  RolledBack --> Cancelled: source residency restored

Only one TransitionId owns the entrance. Commit is idempotent. The transaction revalidates the ant, source residency, both endpoints and arrival; quiesces the source motor; changes residency once; and then hands off the visual binding. Failure restores source residency before releasing occupancy. Inventory, needs, skills, jobs and reservations never transfer by copying.

Requests may be authored while paused, but approach, commit, retries and completion consume no time until resumed. Cancellation during approach leaves the ant in its source region. Cancellation after the commit guard waits for commit or rollback to reach a stable residency.

items.title: View switching
items.text:
sequenceDiagram
  participant H as HUD
  participant V as View coordinator
  participant C as Colony context
  participant W as World context
  participant S as Shared simulation
  H->>V: Choose World View
  V->>C: Save camera pose; disable camera/input
  V->>W: Restore camera pose; enable camera/input
  Note over S: Clock, both loaded regions, ants and jobs continue

Each view remembers camera position and orthographic zoom. Only the active view owns screen-to-local conversion and world input. Colony designation tools are unavailable in World View. Switching never pauses, resumes, orders, cancels, teleports, changes residency or resets a region.

items.title: Surface recommendation
items.text:
WV-B recommendation, still requiring approval:

Item Candidate Initial extent 64×64 logical Surface cells Surface chunk 32×32 cells; four chunks initially resident Layout Fixed seed plus authored entrance, obstacles and nearby sources Movement Top-down open/blocked cells; safe diagonal rule if approved Expansion Missing chunks unavailable; streaming deferred

World terrain does not inherit Colony Background/Solid, gripping, support, falling or local graph rules. Custom World sprites remain unbound until visual and semantic approval.

items.title: Navigation composition and clock
items.text:
A later cross-view route is:

source-local approach → entrance transition → destination-local route.

Each local navigator reports simulated travel cost in its own space. A future cross-view estimate adds source travel, bounded entrance wait/interaction and destination travel. WV-B does not implement autonomous composition; WV-D does.

Both small regions remain loaded and use one SimulationClockController. Pause freezes both regions, transitions, navigation scheduling, needs, interactions, jobs and retry clocks. 1×/2×/3× applies equally. Camera visibility never enables or disables simulation. Reduced-fidelity unloaded simulation is WV-F.

items.title: Seed and water loops
items.text:
flowchart LR
  SS[Finite seed source] -->|direct consume once| H[Hunger restored]
  SS -->|extract after output preflight| P[Recoverable seed parcel]
  P -->|haul| F[Food Storage]
  F -->|reserve and consume| H

  WS[Finite freshwater source] -->|direct drink once| T[Thirst restored]
  WS -->|extract one unit| C[Recoverable water cache]
  C -->|one inventory slot| I[Ant inventory]
  I -->|reserved deposit| W[Water Storage]
  W -->|reserve and consume| T

Sources have stable IDs, Surface locations, resource IDs, remaining integer units, discovery state, revision and exclusive quantity reservations. The first sources are finite and non-regenerating. Discovery changes knowledge only. Depletion and consumption commit exactly once.

Direct eating/drinking requires no storage and creates no cargo. Extraction creates recoverable output and never auto-fills inventory. Seed may use a future generic solid parcel. Water uses a stable one-unit ground cache/payload, never a Soil/Stone drop and never a first-slice stack. Ownership moves atomically through source, cache, inventory and Water Storage. An interruption leaves the unit with its current owner; if no valid release point exists, the ant retains it.

items.title: Natural rest and founding queen
items.text:
A safe natural rest pose must be loaded, clear, locally stable and reachable; must not be an entrance, resource or work anchor; and must be exclusively reserved. Colony poses require Grounded or valid natural grip. Surface poses require traversable non-hazard ground. Critical needs, player order, lifecycle change, invalidated terrain or cancellation interrupt rest without undoing recovery already applied.

Recommended later balance is 8 Fatigue recovery per simulation hour for natural rest versus the existing 16 for a constructed one-ant Sleeping Background. The natural value requires WV-C1 approval. No room quality or new functional capacity is implied.

The generated opening loop is: founding queen starts in the small underground chamber; reaches the linked entrance; survives directly at nearby Surface sources and rests naturally; returns underground; excavates Soil to loose output; personally gathers construction material; builds Sleeping/Food/Water Storage; then extracts and hauls Surface supplies. Storage improves logistics but is not required to obtain survival or the material used to build it. Brood remains later work.

items.title: Milestone gates
items.text:
• WV-B1: typed regions/residency, bounded deterministic Surface, manual camera/input switch, Surface-local movement and one capacity-one round trip.
  • WV-C1: source discovery, finite direct eating/drinking and safe natural rest.
  • WV-C2: seed/water extraction, one-unit liquid payload, hauling and constructed storage.
  • WV-D: bounded autonomous cross-view route composition and work.
  • WV-F: deterministic reduced-fidelity unloaded simulation and reconciliation.

Each gate requires focused Edit Mode invariants, Play Mode integration, manual visual/input acceptance and complete Colony regression preservation. WV-A itself requires documentation validation only.
